headline: Approved loan order to buy 276 Broadway for the senior center, 10-0.
summary: Residents spoke in favor of the senior center purchase. Council members raised questions about debt service and borrowing limits, and the finance chief said the City could work with the debt. Council also referred a request for a draft ordinance on apprenticeship and residency requirements for development projects to the City Manager.
decisions: Approved loan order for land acquisition at 276 Broadway for the senior center, 10 yeas.
Referred to City Manager a request for an update on a draft ordinance on a 25% apprenticeship/residency requirement for development projects.
Referred to City Manager a request for input on asking the State to set criminal penalties for improper ALPR use by authorized users.
Accepted and placed on file the informational report on the zoning rewrite.
Accepted and placed on file the GFOA informational report.
Accepted and placed on file the resignation of Chan Huot from the Lowell Cultural Council.
Adopted acceptance and spending of $115k FY27 earmarked funds for rapid rectangular flash beacons, 9 yeas and 1 absent.
Adopted acceptance and spending of $65,000 FY27 Municipal Road Safety Grant for LPD, 9 yeas and 1 absent.
Adopted and accepted four Boston Gas inspection reports on gas main work.
Referred a property damage claim to the Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred a request for a handicap parking sign at 92 Fort Hill Avenue to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Boston Gas request to replace gas mains at 217-250 Westford Street to a public hearing on November 3, 2026 at 7 PM.
Referred National Grid request for underground electric conduit on Robeson Street to a public hearing on November 3, 2026 at 7 PM.
Referred Zayo request for underground fiber optic conduit at 174 South Street to a public hearing on November 3, 2026 at 7 PM.
Accepted and placed on file the communication on remote and Zoom participation.
Accepted and placed on file the minutes of the October 13 Housing SC and City Council meetings.

4.1. Loan Order - Land Acquisition - 276 Broadway - Senior Center.
In City Council, Given second reading, hearing held.  Motion to adopt and 
refer to Clerk’s Office for 20 days by C. Mercier, seconded by C. Juran.  
Adopted per Roll Call vote 10 yeas (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, C. Juran, M. 
Gitschier, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. 
Scott).  So voted.  The following people spoke in favor of the order: Maxine 
Fargus (opportunity to support seniors with this purchase as the community
grows and there is a need for added space); Richard Demers (noted use of 
the center beyond the seniors); Chris Romero (seniors deserve the City to 
purchase the center); Elaine Pantano (noted other community centers and 
that the City offers so much more); Ryan Faria (noted the better result to 
purchase as opposed to leasing); Linda Sullivan (noted the variety of 
people who visit the center); Jose Cervantes (noted the importance of the 
center for companionship); George and Dottie Hayden (son commented on 
the use of the center benefits his mother greatly); Joanne Alvarez (noted 
she volunteers at the center and that it provides valuable resources); Sheila
Battle (noted center is important to develop friendships); John Somas (it is 
the best interest of the City to keep building where it is and to own it); and 
Edward Cohassett (it would add to improvements in the Acre and provide 
needed services.  There was no one speaking in opposition to the order.
C. Mercier noted the speakers and commented on the importance of the 
senior center to provide necessary services.  C. Robinson noted the 
importance of the center to the senior community and that there is an 
opportunity to seize upon with a new financial structure.  C. Scott noted 
support of the loan order and her concern with the debt service but noted it 
could be managed properly.  C. Scott indicated her prior support for 
expanding the center.  C. McDonough commented on the finances and that
the purchase would include additional spaces.  C. McDonough commented 
on the management of the administration regarding negotiations.  C. Liang 
recognized the difficulty in getting to this point and noted the importance of 
the center to the community.  C. Liang outlined his involvement with the 
senior center for many past years.  C. Juran noted support of the loan order
but must question the financial aspect of it as part of her diligence to the 
taxpayers.  C. Juran questioned process once loan is approved.  Conor

Baldwin (CFO) outlined that process which included filing for 20 days in the 
Clerk’s Office; purchase of property, purchase of bonds to cover loan; and 
budgeting of debt service.  City Solicitor Williams commented on the 
approaching closing date and what is involved in that process.  C. Juran 
questioned the lease of the other two properties involved in the purchase.  
City Solicitor Williams outlined those current leases indicating terms and 
amounts.  C. Juran questioned cap regarding borrowing by the City.  Mr. 
Baldwin noted that there is a cap based on revenues which the City has an 
abundance of space on and that there is a debt service cap the City uses to
ensure sound financial practice.  Mr. Baldwin indicated that they could work
with the debt service though there may be challenges.  C. Descoteaux 
noted the possible realigning CDBG funding.  Mr. Baldwin noted the ability 
to repurpose some of the funds for use in the senior center.  Yovani Baez-
Rose (DPD) outlined the use of formulas to assist with that funding.  Chair 
relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:00 PM.  M. Gitschier noted election 
has consequences and indicated that the three new members made this 
possible today.  M. Gitschier recognized effort of the administration in 
staying the course with the negotiations and gaining leverage.  M. Gitschier 
noted money did not matter in this instance as the senior deserve this.  
Chair returned at 8:10 PM.
Motion by C. Scott, seconded by C. Robinson to take 5-minute recess.  So 
voted.  (8;10 PM).  Roll Call upon return (8:16 PM), 9 present (C. Chau, C. 
Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, 
C. Robinson, C. Scott), 1 absent C. Nuon).
5. CITY COUNCIL - MOTIONS
5.1. C. Robinson - Req. City Mgr. have the proper department provide 
an update on the requested draft ordinance regarding 25% 
apprenticeship/residency requirement on development projects.
In City Council, seconded by C. McDonough, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  Registered speaker, Timothy Collins (commented – City tax dollars 
should pay Lowell residents), addressed the Council.  C. Robinson noted 
the number of times this has been raised and that it is time to take action.  
C. Robinson noted that the demand is there as well as the talent and that

the Council has requested a draft ordinance be presented.  C. McDonough 
noted the amount of upcoming publicly funded projects in the City and that 
should turn into good paying jobs for residents in the City.  
5.2. C. Robinson / M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. have the proper 
department provide input on a path to request the State implement 
criminal penalties on unlawful, improper usage of ALPRs by 
authorized users.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  So voted.  C. 
Robinson noted the concerns and that rules should apply to authorized and 
non-authorized users.  Chair relinquished to Vice Chair Nuon at 6:50 PM.  
M. Gitschier noted the importance of protection in all communities and that 
Lowell could be first to implement this and that the State should follow.  
Chair returned at 6:52 PM.  C. Chau noted this is part of a balance between
safety and privacy.  C. Scott noted other states have such legislation and 
that it is a good deterrent for bad behavior.  C. Descoteaux noted it is an 
important part of transparency.  C. McDonough noted it would be a 
guardrail for bad actors.  
6. COMMUNICATIONS FROM CITY MANAGER
6.1. Informational Reports
Informational Report - Zoning Rewrite - In City Council, Motion “To 
accept and place on file” by C. Mercier, seconded by C. Juran.  So voted.  
Ms. Baez-Rose commented on the status of the zoning rewrite concerning 
both Data Centers and in general, noting future steps would include more 
input.  C. Juran noted the importance of being involved indicating that small
changes could cause large results in different neighborhoods.  C. Juran 
requested Council be given proper lead time to review document before 
public discussion.  C. Robinson requested notice list be very 
comprehensive.  C. Nuon questioned future input for Data Centers and that 
all information be readily available.  Ms. Baez-Rose noted that all 
information is accessible, including options.  C. Descoteaux questioned 
reviewing the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) regulations.  C. Robinson 
noted that there may be a need to revamp the cannabis regulations due to 
changes at state level.
